_about: Spatial rules for the E2 within-prompt study, P05/P08/P15/P16/P23 (v1, approved with edits). Transcribed from prompts.csv text_constrained: only what the text names is a rule; everything else is free (seed-drawn for the recipe). Counts are NOT here (count adherence covers them). Distances are edge-to-edge. A rule with several instances scores the fraction of instances satisfied; spatial adherence = mean over rules. Every scene is scored in the SW-origin frame derived from its own room bounds.
_frame: Room frame: x east (width_m), y north (depth_m), origin at the south-west corner, as P23's text states. The recipe builds around the room centre, so code shifts by (-W/2, -D/2). Walls: north y=D, south y=0, east x=W, west x=0.

_thresholds.near_note: 'by', 'near', 'next to': edge-to-edge distance <= near_m (for a door: to the door opening)
_thresholds.along_wall_note: 'along' a wall (robot cells): footprint edge <= along_wall_m from the wall's inner face
_thresholds.middle_note: 'in the middle': object centre inside the central third of both axes

rules.text: 'two fenced robot cells side by side': adjacent, centres share one axis coordinate within 1.0 m, gap between them <= near_m; wall free
'six workbenches split between both long walls' (long walls = north and south, as 14 > 9): every bench within along_wall_m of the north or south wall, at least 2 on each
'in the middle'

'pallets of returned monitors and desktop PCs near the west door'
'a conveyor running east': axis x, flows to larger x
'four workbenches ... along the conveyor's north side': centre y > conveyor y, centre x inside the conveyor's x span, edge gap <= near_m
'a fenced robot cell at its east end': cell within near_m of the conveyor's east end
'by the east wall': within along_wall_m of the east wall
'next to recycling containers'
'three fenced robot cells along the north wall': all three within along_wall_m of the north wall
'twelve workbenches ... in three rows across the middle': three rows running along x (the long axis), 4 each, row centres inside the central half of y. Orientation along x is my reading of 'across'.
'two shelving units along each of the east and west walls': 2 within along_wall_m of east, 2 of west
'a conveyor from the south door to the central row': one end near_m of the south door, axis y, other end at the central bench row
far end within near_m of the middle bench row
